metadata.name: September 25 and October 8 review regressions
metadata.provenance: Authored after review findings, with source-based labels. A regression suite used during development; not independent annotation, a held-out set, or field accuracy.

cases.description: A local npm alias for LangGraph establishes dependency usage, without proving agent construction.
An ordinary utility installed under an AI package's name is not framework evidence; the npm scheme is case-insensitive.
An ordinary local module shadows the external agents package.

files.app.py:
from agents import Agent
worker = Agent(name="queue worker")

cases.description: An ordinary local package exports a non-AI Agent class.

files.app.py:
from agents import Agent as Worker
worker = Worker(name="queue worker")

cases.description: A qualified call still refers to the repository-local module.
A locally declared Agent is an ordinary class.
A provider completion without model-selected tool dispatch is not an agent.

files.app.py:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()
answer = client.chat.completions.create(model="example", messages=[])

cases.description: Repeated provider calls alone do not establish autonomous tool execution.

files.app.py:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()
for i in range(3):
    response = client.chat.completions.create(model="example", messages=[])
    print(response)

cases.description: Supplying a tool schema without executing a selected tool is not a tool loop.

files.app.py:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()
response = client.chat.completions.create(model="example", messages=[], tools=[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"lookup"}}])
print(response.choices[0].message.tool_calls)

cases.description: Displaying tool-call arguments without dispatch or feedback is not an agent loop.

files.app.py:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()
response = client.chat.completions.create(model="example", messages=[], tools=tools)
for call in response.choices[0].message.tool_calls:
    print(call.function.arguments)

cases.description: An external OpenAI Agents SDK constructor remains recognized.

cases.description: An alias for an external agent constructor remains recognized.

files.app.py:

agent = Assistant(name="assistant", instructions="Help the user")

Author-written October 8 regression: A literal empty comprehension iterable suppresses the unreachable agent construction.

files.app.py:
from agents import Agent
workers = [Agent(name="helper") for _ in []]

cases.description: Author-written October 8 regression: A literal false filter suppresses the unreachable result expression.

files.app.py:
from agents import Agent
workers = [Agent(name="helper") for _ in [1] if False]

cases.description: Author-written October 8 regression: A later empty iterable suppresses the result expression in a nested comprehension.

files.app.py:
from agents import Agent
workers = [Agent(name="helper") for _ in [1] for item in ()]

cases.description: Author-written October 8 regression: The first iterable is evaluated even when a later filter prevents the result.

files.app.py:
from agents import Agent
workers = [item for item in [Agent(name="helper")] if False]

cases.description: Author-written October 8 regression: An earlier filter call is evaluated before a later false filter.

files.app.py:
from agents import Agent
workers = [item for item in [1] if Agent(name="helper") if False]

cases.description: Author-written October 8 regression: A nonempty literal iterable preserves supported constructor evidence.

files.app.py:
from agents import Agent
workers = [Agent(name="helper") for _ in [1]]

Author-written October 8 regression: A standalone .NET tool definition is framework usage.

files.App.cs:
using Microsoft.Extensions.AI;
class App { void Run() { var tool = AIFunctionFactory.Create(Greet); System.Console.WriteLine(tool.Name); } }

cases.description: Author-written October 8 regression: A function-invoking client with concrete nonempty tools and response dispatch establishes an agent candidate.

files.App.cs:
using Microsoft.Extensions.AI;
class App { async System.Threading.Tasks.Task Run(IChatClient inner, AIFunction weather) { var client = new FunctionInvokingChatClient(inner); var options = new ChatOptions { Tools = [weather] }; await client.GetResponseAsync("weather", options); } }

cases.description: Author-written October 8 regression: Automatic invocation without registered tools remains framework usage.

files.App.cs:
using Microsoft.Extensions.AI;
class App { async System.Threading.Tasks.Task Run(IChatClient inner, AIFunction weather) { var client = new FunctionInvokingChatClient(inner); var options = new ChatOptions { Tools = [] }; await client.GetResponseAsync("weather", options); } }

cases.description: Author-written October 8 regression: Mutating a shared tool list invalidates previously registered nonempty tools.

files.App.cs:
using Microsoft.Extensions.AI;
class App { async System.Threading.Tasks.Task Run(IChatClient inner, AIFunction weather) { var client = new FunctionInvokingChatClient(inner); var tools = new List<AITool> { weather }; var options = new ChatOptions { Tools = tools }; tools.Clear(); await client.GetResponseAsync("weather", options); } }
